newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks slump, Dow ends below 8,000 mark.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks slump, Dow ends below 8,000 mark.

text.p: The Dow industrials staggered lower on Tuesday, ending below the 8,000 level for the first time in three weeks after new evidence that U.S. economic growth is accelerating from its tame second quarter pace.
The Dow tumbled 101 points to close unofficially at 7961, the lowest closing for the blue chip average since July 21, when it ended at 7906.72, its last finish below 8,000.

The economic news, which came in the form of a stronger than expected weekly report on U.S. retail sales, dealt a severe blow to the already jittery bond market, which is bracing for a critical monthly sales report due tomorrow.

"People are aware of the potency of (tomorrow's) retail sales number," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities. "They know that a couple of months of buoyant retail sales could change the Fed's mood."
Declining issues outpaced advancing issues by a roughly five-to-four margin on the New York Stock Exchange, on moderate volume of about 500 million shares.
Amgen Inc shares tumbled 6-15/16 to a year low of 50-3/16 after it warned of reduced earnings expectations for its key Epogen drug.
